Chiller stop and automatic backup
counterpart: CH-2 failure detection and automatic failover
para: At 2:10 a.m., when the compressor of CH-2 stops due to overcurrent, the BMS detects the CH-2 stop signal, sends an alarm to the NOC, and automatically starts CH-3, which was on standby.

label: Temperature rise response
para: After starting, CH-3 takes about 8 min to reach its rated cooling capacity, and during that time the average temperature of server room B keeps rising. When the average temperature exceeds 27 °C, the NOC operator moves the non-critical server load of server room B to another server room.

label: Reporting and schedule sharing
para: At 9:00 a.m. the operator sends the customers a report containing the course of the failure and the results of the actions taken, and the facilities team shares the CH-2 replacement schedule with the NOC.

label: Video call after inspection
para: The facilities team, on receiving the NOC's call, arrives on site, inspects the CH-2 compressor, and confirms that the overcurrent relay has tripped. The team shares the symptoms with the manufacturer's remote support center via video call and receives a diagnosis of compressor motor winding damage.

label: Perform virtual machine migration and turning off lights at the same time
para: At 2:16 a.m., when the average temperature reaches 27.5 °C, the operator, in consultation with the customer support team, migrates the virtual machines of 80 non-critical servers to server room A, and at the same time turns off the lighting and humidifiers of server room B to reduce heat generation.

label: Determine response time 200 ms or less
para: Virtual machine migration proceeds 10 servers at a time, and after each migration it is checked whether the service response time is 200 ms or less. If the response time exceeds the threshold, the operator stops the migration, identifies the cause, and then resumes.

label: Remain inoperable until part arrives
para: Because a compressor with damaged windings cannot be repaired on site, the facilities team orders a replacement part from the manufacturer and marks CH-2 as inoperable until the part arrives. Part arrival takes about 3 days.

label: Discard plan when part replacement is complete
para: According to the contingency plan, if only one chiller remains, the operator shuts down all non-critical servers in server room B, notifies the customers, and then keeps only the critical servers running. This plan is discarded once the part replacement is complete.

label: Server room B setpoint at 22 °C

Response lifting and reporting
para: At 9:00 p.m., when the raw water turbidity drops below 30 NTU, the central control room lifts the high-turbidity response stage and returns the monitoring interval to 30 min.

label: Turbidity measurement
para: When the raw water quality analyzer measures a turbidity of 50 NTU and transmits it to the central control room, the central control room declares the high-turbidity response stage. If the turbidity is 100 NTU or more, the central control room temporarily suspends water intake.

label: Transmit after measurement
para: When the raw water quality analyzer measures a turbidity of 50 NTU and transmits it to the central control room, the central control room declares the high-turbidity response stage. If the turbidity is 100 NTU or more, the central control room temporarily suspends water intake.

label: Suspend water intake at 100 NTU or more
para: At 3:00 p.m., when the turbidity is measured at 120 NTU, the central control room temporarily suspends water intake and requests a water supply adjustment from the city hall water supply division.

label: Check level while water intake is suspended
para: While water intake is suspended, the operators check the distribution reservoir level every 30 min. If the distribution reservoir level falls below 40%, the operators open the emergency interconnection pipe.

label: Water treatment plant Response stage Normal
para: At 1:00 p.m., the upstream dam management office notifies the central control room that it will increase the discharge rate. The central control room shortens the raw water turbidity monitoring interval from 30 min to 5 min.

label: Water treatment plant Response stage High-turbidity response
para: When the raw water quality analyzer measures a turbidity of 50 NTU and transmits it to the central control room, the central control room declares the high-turbidity response stage. If the turbidity is 100 NTU or more, the central control room temporarily suspends water intake.

label: Water intake State In operation
para: When the raw water quality analyzer measures a turbidity of 50 NTU and transmits it to the central control room, the central control room declares the high-turbidity response stage. If the turbidity is 100 NTU or more, the central control room temporarily suspends water intake.

label: Water intake State Temporarily suspended

counterpart: Outage cause investigation and evacuation advisory assessment
para: If the load factor of emergency generator No. 1 is 90% or more, the BEMS additionally starts emergency generator No. 2. At 6:40 p.m., when the load factor rises to 92%, the BEMS starts emergency generator No. 2.

label: 2 emergency generators
counterpart: actions:Detect emergency generator No. 1 load factor at 92%
para: The high-rise building operation system consists of the disaster prevention center, the building energy management system (BEMS), 2 emergency generators, 24 elevators, and the emergency broadcast system. The BEMS monitors power usage by floor.

label: Inquiry about cause of power outage
para: At 6:10 p.m., when the external power supply is cut off, the BEMS detects the power outage and automatically starts emergency generator No. 1. The disaster prevention center inquires with KEPCO about the cause of the power outage.

label: Rescue result report
para: The elevator maintenance team manually lowers the 3 elevators one after another to the nearest floor, opens the doors, and rescues the passengers. Each time a rescue is finished, the maintenance team reports the result to the disaster prevention center.

label: Reply with cause of power outage and expected restoration time
para: KEPCO replies to the disaster prevention center that a circuit breaker failure at a nearby substation is the cause and that restoration will take about 1 h.

label: Request rescue after status query
para: The disaster prevention center queries the status of the 24 elevators and identifies 3 stopped elevators. The disaster prevention center requests rescue from the elevator maintenance team and makes a guidance announcement to the trapped passengers through the emergency broadcast system.

label: Reply after inquiry
para: KEPCO replies to the disaster prevention center that a circuit breaker failure at a nearby substation is the cause and that restoration will take about 1 h.

label: Determine power outage exceeds 1 h 30 min
para: If the power outage exceeds 1 h 30 min, the facility manager notifies the tenant companies of an advisory to leave work. On this day the power outage ended after 1 h 10 min, so the advisory to leave work was not issued.

label: External power supply state
para: At 6:10 p.m., when the external power supply is cut off, the BEMS detects the power outage and automatically starts emergency generator No. 1. The disaster prevention center inquires with KEPCO about the cause of the power outage.

label: Emergency generation state
para: When emergency generator No. 1 is started, the BEMS switches power so that only emergency loads are supplied, and cuts off general lighting and air conditioning.

label: Elevator stopped state
para: The disaster prevention center queries the status of the 24 elevators and identifies 3 stopped elevators. The disaster prevention center requests rescue from the elevator maintenance team and makes a guidance announcement to the trapped passengers through the emergency broadcast system.

label: Elevator normal operation state
para: The facility manager restarts the 24 elevators one after another, and the disaster prevention center ends the emergency broadcast after confirming that all elevators are operating normally.

para: The high-rise building operation system consists of the disaster prevention center, the building energy management system (BEMS), 2 emergency generators, 24 elevators, and the emergency broadcast system. The BEMS monitors power usage by floor.

label: Inquiry about cause of power outage
para: At 6:10 p.m., when the external power supply is cut off, the BEMS detects the power outage and automatically starts emergency generator No. 1. The disaster prevention center inquires with KEPCO about the cause of the power outage.

label: Rescue result report
para: The elevator maintenance team manually lowers the 3 elevators one after another to the nearest floor, opens the doors, and rescues the passengers. Each time a rescue is finished, the maintenance team reports the result to the disaster prevention center.

label: Cut off general loads after load switchover
para: When emergency generator No. 1 is started, the BEMS switches power so that only emergency loads are supplied, and cuts off general lighting and air conditioning.

label: Manual lowering after rescue request

label: Reply after inquiry
para: KEPCO replies to the disaster prevention center that a circuit breaker failure at a nearby substation is the cause and that restoration will take about 1 h.

label: Confirm normal operation after restart

label: 3 refrigeration units
para: The cold-storage logistics center operations system consists of a warehouse management system (WMS), 3 refrigeration units, 40 temperature sensors, a door controller, and an emergency generator. The temperature sensors measure the freezer room temperature every 5 min.

label: Shipment delay notification
para: While access is restricted, the logistics manager moves the cargo scheduled for shipment to the backup freezer room and notifies the shipper of the shipment delay. The two tasks proceed simultaneously.
